title: Postsynaptic natural-movie reliability gave 4% higher connection odds per SD in two mouse visual cortex EM datasets; presynaptic and assortative reliability effects were not consistent
abstract: Question: is the trial-to-trial reliability of natural-movie responses related to local synaptic connectivity in mouse visual cortex? We tested three hypotheses: reliable neurons receive more connections (H1), make more connections (H2), or connect preferentially to other reliable neurons (H3). Data: MICrONS functional connectomics tables (Ding et al. 2025, v1; 275,681 axon-dendrite proximity pairs, 144 presynaptic and 10,591 postsynaptic neurons, 7,529 connections) and the Allen V1 Deep Dive mouse (EM release 1196; 99,215 pairs among coregistered cells, 193 presynaptic and 515 postsynaptic cells, 1,447 connections). Reliability is the CCmax correlation ceiling from movie repeats, z-scored within imaging strata. Method: logistic regression with presynaptic (H1, H3) or postsynaptic (H2) fixed effects and geometry splines, two-way cluster-robust intervals, cell-level score-permutation tests, and inverse-variance pooling. Results: postsynaptic reliability increased connection odds by 4.2% per SD in MICrONS (95% CI 1.2-7.2%, permutation p = 0.0004) and by 5.2% in V1DD (CI -2.4 to 13.3%, p = 0.21). The pooled odds ratio was 1.043 (1.016-1.072) without heterogeneity. It stayed after control for pair signal correlation (1.032, 1.005-1.060) and for postsynaptic signal coupling (1.038, 1.010-1.066). The effect is about one third of the like-to-like signal-correlation effect. Presynaptic reliability gave no clear effect in either mouse (permutation p = 0.46 and 0.25). The pre x post interaction had opposite signs in the two mice (1.038 and 0.955; heterogeneity p = 0.008), so the data do not support a reliable-neuron rich club. Limitations: observational data with one mouse per dataset; V1DD has soma-distance controls but no proximity measure; the MICrONS presynaptic sample is small and highly reliable; the final model list was set after one exploratory MICrONS estimate; no multiplicity correction.

Bars are 95% two-way cluster-robust intervals. Postsynaptic reliability (H1) is positive in both mice and pooled; presynaptic reliability (H2) is uncertain; the assortativity interaction (H3) has opposite signs in the two mice.
